subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: The Patriot Act
description: A 60-second lesson on The Patriot Act.

hook.text: Six weeks after 9/11, Congress passed the Patriot Act. Most members admit they didn't read it.

buildup.text: The act expanded government power to tap phones, monitor email, and access business records.

discovery.text: Section 215 let the FBI demand 'any tangible thing' relevant to a terrorism investigation.

twist.text: The NSA interpreted 'any tangible thing' to mean the phone records of every American. Every single one.

climax.text: The Patriot Act showed how quickly fear can override privacy protections built over centuries.

punchline.text: Passed in fear. Privacy lost in weeks.

quiz.question: What did Section 215 of the Patriot Act allow?
options: The FBI to demand 'any tangible thing' relevant to terrorism investigations
